title: Mini’s Off-Roadiest Countryman Gains a Proper Set of Hiking Boots for 2027

body_markdown:
Four years after Mini added some off-road flair to its[Countryman](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/mini-countryman/) lineup via the Untamed Edition, it has given the compact crossover the gear it needed. No, we aren’t talking about the newly available (gas-strut-operated!) roof-top tent, or the “exclusive camping collection,” both of which Mini developed with outside specialists for the 2027 model … we’re talking about an updated interior and a new set of tires.


The Mini Countryman Untamed Edition debuted for 2023 as little more than an appearance package. Sure, the 18-inch wheels were a unique design, and the green leather interior was handsome, but the aesthetic flourishes didn’t quite justify the price: almost $10,000 over a base Countryman. Overall, the first rendition of the Untamed Edition didn’t live up to the marketing lingo, which described it as “rugged” and “adventurous, whatever the weather.” The tires were a big reason: The original Untamed Edition was delivered on 225/50R18 Pirelli Cinturato P7 Runflats. Tire Rack describes this model as a “grand touring all season.” Not the sort of rubber that screams, “Take me to the trail!”


Mini is quite proud of this new grille.


Mini / Bernhard Filser

Mini was serious enough that it worked with Pirelli to develop a new set of all-terrain tires for the car. (The press release calls them “all terrain plus” tires.) Part of the Scorpion XTM AT family, they are wider (245 versus 225 mm), with tread blocks that are obviously chunkier. They’re fit to a larger set of alloy wheels (19 versus 18 inches) that, again, are a design unique to the Untamed Edition. To complement the updated wheel-and-tire package, the suspension has received a 15-mm lift. Altogether, the updates increase ground clearance by 19 mm, or about 3/4 of an inch.


2023MY


[Chris Stark](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/chris-stark/)


2027MY


Mini / Bernhard Filser


[One of our biggest complaints](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2023-mini-cooper-s-countryman-all4-untamed-a-cute-ute-that-prefers-to-stay-on-the-leash/) about the 2023 Untamed Edition was the interior, which we found gimmicky. We haven’t sat in the new car yet, but from the photos, the revamped interior looks far more contemporary in its use of color and texture. There are fewer multicolored lights and less black plastic around the display, for starters. The gray and blue knitted textures on the dash and seats complement each other well and succeed in looking more appropriate for the $45,250 sticker price. We’re excited to see if the interior feels as upscale as it looks.


Mini / Bernhard Filser


Mini / Bernhard Filser


Mini / Bernhard Filser


Mini / Bernhard Filser


A quick note on price: The second version of the Untamed Edition is significantly cheaper than the first. At launch, the 2023 car cost $47,750. That’s a difference of $2500—closer to $7000, when you account for inflation. Another complaint we had about the Untamed Edition is addressed!


We’re most curious to see how the wheel/tire/suspension upgrades change the driving experience. They are absolutely necessary if this car is to be at all “adventurous” and “rugged,” but we wonder how they will impact its on-road behavior, which we really enjoyed. Until then, props to Mini for giving its off-roadiest Countryman the equipment it needs to succeed.
